The provided data outlines the demographic and clinical characteristics of patients receiving treatment with [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (BMSL), comparing the pediatric population ("Børn og unge") against the adult population ("Voksne") [^src1]. The adult cohort vastly outnumbers the pediatric group, comprising 10,163 patients compared to just 360 children and adolescents [^src1].

Regarding clinical diagnoses, [[dk50-crohns-sygdom|DK50* Crohns sygdom]] is the leading condition across both demographics, affecting 6,184 adults (61%) and 247 children (69%) [^src1]. [[dk51-ulceroes-colitis|DK51* Ulcerøs colitis]] is the second most common, recorded in 3,931 adults (39%) and 113 children (31%) [^src1]. An outlier in the diagnostic distribution is the presence of primary sclerosing cholangitis (DK830F) and short bowel syndrome (DK912B), which are recorded exclusively in the pediatric cohort with 28 and 20 patients, respectively, while no adults are listed under these specific codes in this table [^src1].

Gender distribution reveals a distinct divergence between the two groups. Among children and adolescents, there is a clear male predominance, with 206 boys (57%) compared to 154 girls (43%) [^src1]. In contrast, the adult population exhibits an almost perfectly even gender split, comprising 5,114 women (50%) and 5,049 men (50%) [^src1].

Age statistics further delineate the cohorts. The pediatric patients have a mean age of 14 years (range 2–17) and a median of 15 years, with 100% of this group naturally falling into the 0–17 years bracket [^src1]. The adult cohort is significantly older, with a mean age of 43 years (range 18–96) and a median of 41 years [^src1]. Within the adult group, the youngest demographic (18–29 years) represents the largest segment with 2,542 patients (25%), while the oldest demographic (90 years or older) is the smallest, comprising only 5 patients (0%) [^src1]. Because this analysis is based on a single dated table section, no longitudinal trends over time can be established.

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner karakteristika for patienter, der modtog BMSL-behandling i perioden, og viser en klar aldersopdeling: alle børn og unge er i 0–17-årsalderen, mens voksne primært er mellem 18 og 59 år, samt en overvægt af mænd blandt børn og en næsten ligelig kønsfordeling blandt voksne.
